questions.question: Under which Amendment Act has the electorate been widened by lowering the age to 18 years?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is the __**61st**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **61st Amendment Act of the Constitution** of India is officially known as The Constitution (Sixty-first Amendment) Act, 1988.
 
• It **lowered the voting age of elections to the Lok Sabha and legislative assemblies from 21 years to 18 years**.
 
• This amendment brought a major change to the Indian political system by making it more inclusive and allowing the youth to participate in the electoral process.
 
• The rationale behind the reduction of the voting age was that if an individual can be allowed to marry and have a family at the age of 18, the individual should be also considered mature enough to be given voting rights.
 
• Young people, constituting a large section of the population, should therefore play a vital role in the electoral process.
 
• The Constitution (Sixty-first Amendment) Bill, 1988 was introduced in the Lok Sabha on December 13, 1988.
 
• This amendment is deemed to have been in effect from March 28, 1989.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **76th Amendment Act** was related to the **reservation of seats for Scheduled Tribes in the State of Tripura, Mizoram, and Arunachal Pradesh**.
 
• The **42nd Amendment Act** officially known as '**The Constitution of India (42nd Amendment) Act, 1976**'.
 
• This amendment, often called the "Mini Constitution," brought about the most widespread changes to the Constitution in India's history, including changes to the Preamble and several other key areas.
 
• The **72nd Amendment Act** deals with the **special provisions for the State of Sikkim**.

questions.question: What does air drainage do in cold climate?

options.text: It protects plants from frost damages.
It filters out better quality air.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It protects plants from frost damages**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Air drainage in a cold climate is an essential factor in preventing damage to vegetation, especially sensitive plants, from frost.
 
• **Air drainage refers to the movement of air from higher to lower areas, following the laws of gravity**.
 
• On a cold night, **denser cold air tends to descend into lower areas, displacing warmer air**.
 
• If this colder air accumulates and remains stagnant, it can lead to the creation of frost, causing damage to plant tissue.
 
• In areas with good air drainage, this **cold air continues to move down the slope rather than accumulating in one space**, thus reducing the likelihood of frost forming and consequently protecting plants from frost damage.
 
• Therefore, proper site selection considering topography and air drainage can be an important factor in mitigating frost damage in agricultural or horticultural contexts in cold climates.
 
• **While air movement can affect dust particles, air drainage does not specifically target dust elevation.**
 
• **Air drainage, doesn't have a direct impact on soil temperature. It might indirectly affect it by modifying the microclimate.**
 
• **Air drainage doesn't filter air to improve its quality. It refers to the natural movement of air due to differences in temperature and elevation.**
 
• **Hence, option 2 is the correct answer.**

questions.question: Which of the following is a mathematical expression of Dalton's partial pressure law? (Where P = Pressure, T = Temperature, V = Volume, n = number of moles)

options.text: pTₒₜₐₗ = p₁ + p₂ + p₃ + _____ (at constant T, P)
pTotal = p₁ + p₂ + p₃ + _____ (at constant T, n)
pTotal = p₁ + p₂ + p₃ + _____ (at constant V, P)
pTotal = p₁ + p₂ + p₃ + _____ (at constant T, V)

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __pTotal = p1 + p2 + p3 + _____ (at constant T, V)__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **John Dalton's Law of Partial Pressures **is often referred to as Dalton's Law. 
 
• It states that in a mixture of non-reacting gases, the total pressure exerted is equal to the sum of the partial pressures of the individual gases.
 
• Mathematically,** if a gas mixture contains gases 1, 2, 3, and so on, the total pressure (pTotal) would be the sum of the pressures that each would exert if it were alone (p1, p2, p3, etc).**
 
• This is generally true for a system **at constant temperature (T) and volume (V)**. Changes in temperature or volume could lead to changes in the pressure.
 
• Hence, when adding the partial pressures of gases to determine the total pressure of the system, it's necessary to hold temperature and volume constant.
 
• Dalton's law predicts the behavior of gases in physical phenomena such as air pressure and scuba diving.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• **Charles' Law**

 
 
• Charles's Law, named after Jacques Charles, is a principle in the field of gas physics.
 
• It simply states that for a given amount of gas **at a consistent pressure, the volume is directly proportional to its absolute temperature.**
 
• In other words, as temperature increases, the volume of the gas expands, and as the temperature decreases, the volume contracts.
 
• This occurs because increased temperature provides gas particles with more kinetic energy, causing them to move and collide more, thereby occupying more space.
 
• Meanwhile, reducing the temperature causes the particles to slow down and take up less space.
 
• The mathematical expression of **Charles's Law is V₁/T₁ = V₂/T₂, where V represents volume, T represents absolute temperature (in Kelvin), and the subscripts 1 and 2 refer to the initial and final states, respectively.**
 
• This equation helps predict how gases will behave under various thermal conditions.
 
• Charles's Law has practical applications in various fields, including meteorology, hot-air ballooning, engineering, and many more.
 
 
 
• **Boyle's Law**
 
 
• Boyle's Law, named after physicist Robert Boyle, is a fundamental concept in the field of gas physics.
 
• It states that at a constant temperature, **the pressure and volume of a fixed amount of gas are inversely proportional.**
 
• This relationship implies that if you increase the pressure exerted on a gas, its volume decreases and vice versa, given the temperature remains constant.
 
• In mathematical terms, **Boyle's Law can be expressed as P₁V₁ = P₂V₂, where P represents pressure, V represents volume, and subscripts 1 and 2 represent the initial and final states, respectively.**
 
• Boyle’s Law is essentially a statement about collisions. It holds because the gas pressure is produced by molecules colliding with the walls of the container.
 
• If the volume of the container is reduced, the gas molecules will hit the walls more frequently, thereby increasing the pressure.
 
• In practical terms, Boyle's Law helps understand the function of a syringe in medicine, the compression of gas in engines, and deep-sea diving where pressure changes significantly with depth. 
 
 
 
• **Gay - Lussac's Law**
 
 
• Gay-Lussac's Law was named after the French chemist Joseph Louis Gay-Lussac.
 
• It is a gas law that states **the pressure of a gas directly varies with the temperature, provided the volume stays constant.**
 
• Essentially, when a gas is heated, its pressure increases, and conversely, when it's cooled, the pressure decreases.
 
• The mathematical expression of **Gay-Lussac's law is P₁/T₁ = P₂/T₂, where P stands for pressure, T for absolute temperature (in Kelvin), and the numbers 1 and 2 correspond to the initial and final states.**
 
• The explanation lies in kinetic theory: when you heat a gas, its particles gain energy, causing them to move more swiftly and collide more frequently and forcefully with the container walls, leading to higher pressure.
 
• Conversely, cooling the gas slows down the particles, reducing the number and intensity of collisions, thereby decreasing the pressure.
 
• Gay-Lussac's Law helps explain phenomena such as why pressure cooker works efficiently, or why an aerosol can explode if left in a hot car.

questions.concept: India under East India Company’s Rule
questions.question: Who decided to go ahead with his plans of invasion of Afghanistan resulting in the first Anglo-Afghan War?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lord Auckland**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **first Anglo-Afghan War** took place from **1839 to 1842**.
 
• It was one of the first major conflicts during the "Great Game," the 19th-century competition for **power and influence in Central Asia between the United Kingdom and Russia**.
 
• The **decision to invade Afghanistan was made by George Eden, Earl of Auckland,** also known as Lord Auckland.
 
• He was serving as **Governor-General of India at the time**. Lord Auckland's proclamation issuing the invasion, often referred to as the **"Simla Manifesto",** was issued on October 1, 1838.
 
• His plans for the invasion were prompted by fears of growing Russian influence in Afghanistan and threats to India, then a part of the British Empire.
 
• Auckland's strategy was to replace the existing ruler, Dost Mohammad Khan, with a pro-British monarch, Shah Shuja.
 
• This plan ultimately ended in failure and backlash, leading to what is often considered one of the greatest military humiliations of the British Empire.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Edward Law, Earl of Ellenborough, replaced Lord Auckland as Governor-General of India and it fell upon him to resolve the debacle of the First Anglo-Afghan War.
 
• James Ramsay, Earl of Dalhousie, served much later and was Governor-General of India from 1848 to 1856. He is known for his policy of annexation, the doctrine of lapse, and for introducing railways and telegraph to India.
 
• Edward Robert Bulwer-Lytton, served as the Viceroy of India from 1876 to 1880. His tenure is known for the controversial Vernacular Press Act and the controversial handling of the Great Famine of 1876–78.

questions.question: Who accidentally discovered the synthesis of ether in 1850, by reacting alcohols with alkyl iodides in the presence of sulphuric acid?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Alexander William Williamson**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Alexander William Williamson** was a British chemist who, while performing studies on ethers, accidentally discovered its synthesis.
 
• This happened during a series of experiments in the mid-19th century, specifically in the year 1850.
 
• He found that **when he reacted alcohols with alkyl iodides in the presence of sulfuric acid, ethers were formed**.
 
• This is now** recognized as the Williamson Ether Synthesis**, named after him.
 
• This reaction is still widely used for the preparation of ethers and has considerable importance in organic chemistry.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Carl Wilhelm Scheele** was a Swedish pharmaceutical chemist credited with the **discovery of several chemical substances, including oxygen** (though Joseph Priestley published his findings first).
 
• **Jabir Ibn Hayyan **was a prominent polymath during the Islamic Golden Age.
 
• Often described as the** "father of early chemistry," **he introduced a scientific and experimental approach to alchemy and made significant contributions to areas like the classification of substances, alkalis, and distillation techniques.
 
• However, ether synthesis was not part of his discoveries.

• **Panchayatana is a style of temple architecture** that surfaced in India during the time of the **Gupta Empire**, and its literal meaning is **"five shrines"**.
 
• The main hallmark of this style is the presence of **four subsidiary shrines positioned at the corners around a larger, central shrine**.
 
• Hence, a Panchayatana temple complex consists of five shrines in total—four at the corners and one in the middle.
 
• This style represents the central doctrine of the **Smarta sect of Hinduism**, which regards the worship of multiple deities as different paths leading to the same Brahman or the ultimate reality.

questions.question: In 1910, who applied the newly developed method of radioactive dating to minerals in the first attempt to quantitatively estimate the age of the Earth?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Arthur Holmes**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Arthur Holmes** was a British geologist who made pivotal contributions to the study of the age of the Earth.
 
• His work established the basis for the geological timescale, which is commonly used today.
 
• **In 1910, Holmes**, then a student, **made one of the earliest uses of radioactive dating to study the age of the Earth - he did this by applying radioactivity to the dating of rocks**.
 
• Holmes used uranium-lead dating to analyze a mineral, known as pitchblende.
 
• The quantitative results were not precise by today's standards, but this marked a significant first step in chronometric dating in geology, and Holmes remained a major advocate for radioactive methods in geochronology.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Friedrich Mohs** was a German geologist and mineralogist, best known for developing the **Mohs scale of mineral hardness**, a qualitative scale characterizing scratch resistance of various minerals.
 
• **Clair C Patterson** was an American geochemist, Patterson developed the **uranium-lead dating method into lead-lead dating** and, by using lead isotopic data from the Canyon Diablo meteorite, **he calculated an age for the Earth of 4.55 billion years**, which is very close to the currently accepted age.
 
• **Alfred Wegenerwas** a German polar researcher, geophysicist, and meteorologist, Wegener is best known for his **theory of continental drift** (that the continents slowly move across the Earth's surface), later replaced by the theory of plate tectonics.

questions.question: Which of the following measures of money supply is considered least liquid?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **M4**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Broad money** is a category for measuring the** amount of money circulating in an economy**. 
 
• It is defined as the most **inclusive method **of calculating a given country's money supply. 
 
• Central banks tend to keep tabs on broad money growth to help forecast inflation.
 
• Central banks often look at broad money, alongside narrow money, to set monetary policy.
 
• The value of the currency depreciates as inflation rises. This is why the RBI keeps track of the money supply by categorizing it as ‘reserve money,’ ‘narrow money,’ and ‘broad money. 
 
• Money supply refers to the total amount of money in circulation among the general population at any one moment. M1, M2, M3, and **M4 **are the four money supply measurements released by the RBI.
 
• **M1** includes money in circulation plus checkable deposits in banks.
 
• **M2** includes M1 plus savings deposits and money market mutual funds.
 
• **M3** includes M2 plus large-time deposits in banks. 
 
• **M0** includes the narrowest forms, and **M4 includes the broadest forms – M0/M1/M2/M3/M4.**

questions.question: The weather in India, during winter months, is impacted by the distribution of surface pressure from ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Central and Western Asia**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the **winter months**, the weather conditions over India are generally influenced by the **distribution of pressure in Central and Western Asia**.
 
• A **high-pressure center** in the region lying to the north of the Himalayas develops during winter.
 
• This center of high pressure gives rise to the **flow of air** at the **low level** from the** north** towards the **Indian subcontinent**, south of the mountain range.
 
• The **surface winds** blowing out of the high-pressure center over **Central Asia** reach India in the form of a **dry continental air mass**.
 
• These continental winds come in contact with trade winds over northwestern India.
 
• The position of this **contact zone** is not, however, stable. Occasionally, it may shift its position as far** east** as the **middle Ganga valley** with the result that the whole of northwestern and northern India up to the middle Ganga valley comes under the influence of **dry northwestern winds**. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Jet Stream and Upper Air Circulation**:

 
 
• The pattern of **air circulation** discussed above is witnessed only at the** lower level** of the atmosphere near the surface of the earth.
 
• Higher up in the lower troposphere, about three km above the surface of the earth, a different pattern of air circulation is observed.
 
• The variations in the atmospheric pressure closer to the surface of the earth have no role to play in the making of upper air circulation.
 
• All of **Western and Central Asia** remains under the influence of **westerly winds** along with an altitude of **9-13 km** from **west to east**.
 
• These winds blow across the **Asian continent** at latitudes north of the Himalayas roughly parallel to the Tibetan highlands. These are known as **jet streams**.
 
• **Tibetan highlands **act as a barrier in the path of these** jet streams**. As a result, jet streams get bifurcated. One of its branches blows to the north of the Tibetan highlands, while the southern branch blows in an eastward direction, south of the Himalayas.
 
• It has its mean position at** 25°N in February at 200-300 MB** level. It is believed that this southern branch of the** jet stream exercises** an important** influence** on the **winter weather** in India.

questions.question: Select the INCORRECT statement about HDL.

options.text: It absorbs cholesterol in the blood and carries it back to the liver.
It is considered as good cholesterol.
High levels of HDL cholesterol raise the risk for heart disease and stroke.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **High levels of HDL cholesterol raise the risk for heart disease and stroke**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Cholesterol
 
 
• It is produced in the body and builds membranes around the cell in order to protect it.
 
• It is a chemical compound that is waxy in nature.
 
• The liver produces cholesterol, it is found in red fat meat, cheese, butter, and eggs.
 
• Lipoprotein helps in the transport of these through the blood. Increased cholesterol levels are not good for health as it causes cardiovascular disease.
 
• Cholesterol is insoluble in blood, it is transported in the circulatory system within lipoproteins.
 
• There are several types of lipoproteins in the blood very-low-density lipoprotein (VLDL), intermediate-density lipoprotein (IDL), low-density lipoprotein (LDL), and high-density lipoprotein (HDL).
 
• LDL cholesterol is considered bad cholesterol because it contributes to fatty buildup in arteries. This condition narrows the arteries and increases the risk of heart attack, Stroke, and peripheral artery disease or PAD.
 
• HDL cholesterol can be thought of as the good cholesterol. So in the case of HDL cholesterol, higher levels are actually better.
 
• HDL acts as a scavenger, carrying LDL (bad) cholesterol away from the arteries and back to the liver, where the LDL is broken down and passed from the body.
 
• A healthy HDL cholesterol level may protect against heart attack and stroke. low levels of HDL cholesterol increase the risk of heart disease.

• HDL cholesterol picks up excess cholesterol floating in our blood and takes it to our liver where it is broken down and removed from our body.
 
• It is called Good Cholesterol.

• LDL makes up most of our body’s cholesterol. High levels of LDL can lead to a build-up of cholesterol in arteries.
 
• Sometimes, a clot can also be formed leading to a high risk of stroke/heart attack in adults.
 
 
 
 

 
 
Triglyceride

 
 
 
 
• Triglyceride is a type of fat (lipid) and is a major source of energy for the food.
 
• High level of Triglyceride can harden the arteries or it can thicken the artery walls which increase the risk of stroke and heart disease.
 
 
 
 

 
 
Fatty Acids

 
 
 
 
• During digestion, the body breaks down fats into fatty acids.
 
• Fatty acids are the building blocks of the fat in our bodies. When glucose (as an energy source) is not available in the body, the fatty acid is used by the body to provide energy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__ **

__
 
• The Regulating Act of 1773 set the cornerstone for centralization.
 
• In British India, the Charter Act of 1833 was seen as the culmination of the process of centralization.
 
• The Saint Helena Act of 1833 and the Government of India Act of 1833 are other names for it.
 
• The East India Company's Charter Act, of 1813, was renewed by an act of the British Parliament.
 
• The EIC's charter was extended by this law for another 20 years.
 
• The East India Company had its trade privileges taken away.
 
• Features of the Charter Act of 1833:
 
 
• The company's commercial activities were closed down, it was made into an administrative body
 
• The company's trade links with China were closed down
 
• This act legalized the British colonization of the country 
 
• Provision
 
 
• The Governor-general of Bengal was re-designated as the Governor-General of India
 
• Lord William Bentinck was the first governor-general of India 
 
• The governor-general had legislative power over the entire British India.
 
 
 
• Significance of the Charter Act of 1833
 
 
• It was the first step in the centralization of India's administration.

• **The Charter Act of 1813** passed by the British Parliament renewed the East India Company's charter for another 20 years. This is also called the East India Company Act, of 1813. This act is important in that it defined for the first time the constitutional position of British Indian territories.
 
• **The Charter Act 1793**, or **commonly the East India Company Act 1793** was passed by the British Parliament to renew the charter of the East India Company, which authorized the company to carry on their monopolistic trade in India for the next 20 years, which was earlier given to it by the Regulating Act in 1773.
